drivingQuestion: How can Rabban Gamliel say 'and not only did they say' about a midnight limit he does not hold?
outcomeNote: The mishna's wording is explained: Rabban Gamliel spoke from within the Rabbis' formulation.

segments.he: וְרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מִי קָאָמַר ״עַד חֲצוֹת״ דְּקָתָנֵי ״וְלֹא זוֹ בִּלְבַד אָמְרוּ״?
segments.en: The Gemara questions the formulation of the mishna: «Does Rabban Gamliel say until midnight, that he teaches: And not only did they say?» Rabban Gamliel does not restrict the time for the recitation of Shema until midnight, so why does he say, and not only do they say, implying that he agrees with that stringency?

segments.he: הָכִי קָאָמַר לְהוּ רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לִבְנֵיהּ: אֲפִילּוּ לְרַבָּנַן דְּקָאָמְרִי ״עַד חֲצוֹת״, מִצְוָתָהּ עַד שֶׁיַּעֲלֶה עַמּוּד הַשַּׁחַר. וְהַאי דְּקָא אָמְרִי עַד חֲצוֹת — כְּדֵי לְהַרְחִיק אָדָם מִן הָעֲבֵירָה.
segments.en: The Gemara explains that «this is what Rabban Gamliel said to his sons: Even according to the Rabbis, who say» that the mitzva may be performed only «until midnight,» the biblical obligation to perform «the mitzva» continues «until dawn, and that which they say» that it may only be recited «until midnight» is «in order to distance a person from transgression.»

moves.cueHe: ורבן גמליאל מי קאמר ״עד חצות״ דקתני ״ולא זו בלבד אמרו״?
moves.summary: objects to the mishna's wording, since Rabban Gamliel never set a midnight limit
moves.about: Rabban Gamliel never said 'until midnight', so the mishna's wording 'and not only did they say' misfits his own position

moves.cueHe: הכי קאמר להו רבן גמליאל לבניה
moves.summary: reconstrues him as speaking on the Rabbis' terms: even for them the mitzva runs to dawn, midnight being a fence
moves.about: what Rabban Gamliel meant is that even on the Rabbis' view the mitzva runs until dawn, midnight being only a fence

edges.about: what Rabban Gamliel meant is that even on the Rabbis' view the mitzva runs until dawn, midnight being only a fence
on the reconstrued reading, Rabban Gamliel grants that even the Rabbis hold the biblical time runs to dawn, their midnight limit being a safeguard
